_description_listen_dns: IP:port for the plain DNS (UDP and TCP) listener. Must be an IP literal, never a hostname.
_description_listen_doh: IP:port for the local DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) listener. Must be an IP literal. A TLS certificate is auto-generated for this IP.
_description_listen_ui: IP:port for the web admin UI. Must be a specific interface IP literal (not the 0.0.0.0/:: wildcard, which would make the WebUI unreachable). TLS is auto-enabled for non-loopback addresses when webui_force_tls_on_non_localhost is true.
_description_tls_cert_file: filename(no path!) of the TLS certificate file (PEM format), stored next to config.json, used for local DoH and WebUI. Auto-generated as self-signed, if not on-disk.
_description_tls_key_file: filename(no path!) of the TLS private key file (PEM format), stored next to config.json, used for local DoH and WebUI. Auto-generated as self-signed, if not on-disk.
_description_upstream_urls: HTTPS URLs of upstream DoH resolvers (e.g. https://9.9.9.9/dns-query). Must use IP literals. Order determines failover priority. If you use the template '{builtin:clientexe}'(without the single quotes, doh) it will be replaced with the querying executable name (useful for NextDNS URLs)
_description_upstream_sni_hostnames: TLS SNI hostnames corresponding to each upstream_urls entry (e.g. dns.quad9.net). Falls back to the URL host if omitted or shorter than upstream_urls.
_description_upstream_selection_mode: Strategy for querying upstreams: 'failover' (sticky, auto-heals), 'fastest' (race all, first valid wins), 'strict' (all must agree or query is dropped).
_description_upstream_retries_per_query: Additional retry attempts after the first try fails (0 = no retries; total tries = 1 + this value).
_description_block_mode: Action for blocked queries: 'nxdomain' (return NXDOMAIN), 'ip_block' (return block_ip/block_ipv6 addresses), 'drop' (for DoH clients it actually replies with 503 Service Unavailable, otherwise it will just cause long waits/timeouts for clients by not replying anything, TODO: maybe remove this drop mode).
_description_whitelist_mode: If true (default), the default policy is deny-all-except-whitelisted: a query is only allowed if it matches an enabled whitelist rule (or a local host override). If false, the default policy is allow-all-except-blocklisted: whitelist rules play no role in the allow/deny decision and every query is allowed by default. In BOTH modes the query blocklist (query_blocklist_file / query_blocklist_external_hosts_file) is always checked first and always takes priority over this policy, and the response-IP blacklist is always applied to the actual returned IPs regardless of mode.
_description_block_ip: IPv4 address returned for blocked A queries when block_mode is 'ip_block' (typically 0.0.0.0).
_description_block_ipv6: IPv6 address returned for blocked AAAA queries when block_mode is 'ip_block' (typically ::).
_description_qps_rate_globally: Maximum DNS queries per second across all clients combined (token-bucket sustained rate).
_description_qps_burst_globally: Maximum burst of DNS queries allowed globally above the sustained qps_rate_globally limit.
_description_qps_rate_per_client: Maximum DNS queries per second allowed from a single client IP.
_description_qps_burst_per_client: Maximum burst of DNS queries allowed from a single client IP above qps_rate_per_client.
_description_webui_qps_rate_globally: Maximum WebUI HTTP requests per second across all clients combined (token-bucket sustained rate). Independent of qps_rate_globally, which only governs DNS query traffic.
_description_webui_qps_burst_globally: Maximum burst of WebUI HTTP requests allowed globally above the sustained webui_qps_rate_globally limit.
_description_webui_qps_rate_per_client: Maximum WebUI HTTP requests per second allowed from a single client IP.
_description_webui_qps_burst_per_client: Maximum burst of WebUI HTTP requests allowed from a single client IP above webui_qps_rate_per_client.
_description_cache_min_ttl: Minimum TTL (seconds) for any cached DNS response, overriding lower upstream TTLs. 0 means no minimum (upstream TTL is respected, which if 0 means don't cache).
_description_cache_max_entries: Maximum DNS cache entries. New entries are silently dropped when the limit is reached until expired entries are evicted.
_description_whitelist_file: filename(no path!) of the query-whitelist JSON file, stored next to config.json. Created automatically with an empty whitelist if absent. Only consulted when whitelist_mode is true; the query blocklist is always checked first and always takes priority over these rules.
_description_blacklist_file: filename(no path!) of the response-IP blacklist JSON file, stored next to config.json. Created automatically with safe defaults if absent.
_description_hosts_file: filename(no path!) of the local host-override JSON file, stored next to config.json. Resolved locally without needing to match the whitelist rules first. The query blocklist is checked before this and takes priority over it, unless local_hosts_override_query_blocklist is true.
_description_query_blocklist_file: filename(no path!) of the dnsbollocks-owned, mutable query-blocklist override JSON file, stored next to config.json. Holds 'block' patterns (always block a query outright, regardless of whitelist_mode or any whitelist rule) and 'except' patterns (cancel a block coming ONLY from query_blocklist_external_hosts_file — never from a 'block' pattern here, and never bypassing the normal whitelist/default policy on their own). Always checked first, before whitelist rules and local host overrides (see local_hosts_override_query_blocklist). Created automatically with an empty ruleset if absent.
_description_query_blocklist_external_ho: optional path to a read-only, standard hosts-file (e.g. StevenBlack Hosts) used as an additional query-blocklist source; unlike other file settings this is NOT restricted to a bare filename (it can be absolute, or relative to the working directory) since dnsbollocks never writes to it. Syntax per line: '<IPv4|IPv6> <host> [<alias> ...]'; '#' starts a comment through end-of-line, even mid-line. Only lines whose mapping IP is the unspecified address (0.0.0.0 or ::) contribute hostnames to the block set — this is the conventional blocklist signal used by StevenBlack Hosts and similar files. Lines with any other mapping IP (e.g. 127.0.0.1 localhost, ::1 localhost, 255.255.255.255 broadcasthost) are deliberately ignored for blocking (still counted/logged as non-standard) so ordinary hosts-file loopback/broadcast entries never false-positive-block. The mapped IP is never used as a DNS answer from this layer; intentional local overrides belong in hosts_file. Matches exact hostnames only (no wildcards) — put dnsbollocks-specific wildcard patterns in query_blocklist_file instead. Empty (default) disables this layer entirely. A local 'except' pattern in query_blocklist_file can cancel a block coming from this file, but never bypasses whitelist_mode/whitelist rules on its own.
_description_local_hosts_override_query_: If false (default), the query blocklist (query_blocklist_file / query_blocklist_external_hosts_file) is checked before local host overrides (hosts_file), so a blocklisted domain stays blocked even if it also has a local host override. If true, a matching local host override is resolved directly and the query blocklist is skipped entirely for that query.
_description_log_dir: Directory where all log files will be saved. Can be absolute or relative(to config dir). If empty aka "" then it defaults_to/uses config dir(which is current directory when exe was started). Log file names will be stripped of any folder paths and forced into this directory.
_description_log_queries: filename(no path!) to the DNS query-only log file (JSON lines). Created automatically.
_description_log_queries_simple: filename(no path!) to a simple, plain-text (non-JSON) per-query log file: one line per query formatted as 'timestamp type domain action ips-list'. Created automatically. Complements log_queries for fast human scanning; cross-reference the identical timestamp in log_queries for exe/protocol/rule-id/timing details.
_description_log_file: filename(no path!) to the full system log file (JSON lines, all levels including debug). Created automatically.
_description_console_log_level: Minimum log level printed to the console: 'debug', 'info', 'warn', or 'error'. File logs always receive all levels.
_description_log_max_size_mb: Maximum log file size in megabytes before rotation. Rotated files are renamed with a sequential numeric suffix (.1, .2, ...).
_description_allow_run_as_admin: If false (default), the process exits immediately when running with Windows administrator privileges as a safety guardrail.
_description_hide_console: If true, detaches from the console window entirely at startup (equivalent in effect to a -H=windowsgui build)(for max.effect run it from a .lnk not from a .bat unless you append an & in the .bat): no console window is shown and no console I/O is possible for the remainder of this run. Interactive features (initial password-setup prompt, Ctrl+R/Ctrl+X/Ctrl+C/Alt+V keyboard shortcuts) become unavailable once detached, so webui_password_hash must already be set beforehand (e.g. run --hash-password once with this off first). Use the WebUI instead: Apply & Reload replaces Ctrl+R, and the Shutdown button on the Stats page replaces Ctrl+X. Logging continues to the configured log files unaffected. Re-checked only at startup, never on reload; toggling this requires a full process restart to take effect.
_description_block_aaaa_as_empty_noerror: Return NOERROR with an empty answer for blocked AAAA queries instead of NXDOMAIN, preventing Windows from caching the domain as non-existent and breaking IPv4 fallback (e.g. ssh to github.com).
_description_allow_https_if_a_allowed: If true, an HTTPS-type DNS query is automatically allowed whenever an A-type whitelist rule permits the same domain, without needing a separate HTTPS rule.
_description_remove_https_ip_hints: Strip ipv4hint and ipv6hint parameters from HTTPS DNS records in upstream responses, forcing clients to resolve IPs via A/AAAA queries instead of using embedded hints.
_description_use_ede_in_blocked_reply: Attach an EDNS0 Extended DNS Error (EDE) record to blocked responses so clients and diagnostic tools can see a human-readable reason for the block.
_description_webui_password_hash: Bcrypt hash of the web admin UI password. Set via --hash-password flag or the WebUI config page. Never store a plaintext password here.
_description_webui_password_bcrypt_cost: Bcrypt cost factor used when hashing new passwords (minimum enforced: 4, max is 31). Higher values are slower but more resistant to brute-force.
_description_webui_use_tls: Serve the web admin UI over HTTPS using the auto-generated self-signed certificate. Strongly recommended for any non-loopback address.
_description_webui_force_tls_on_non_loca: Automatically promote webui_use_tls to true when listen_ui is bound to a non-loopback address, preventing the password from being transmitted as plaintext.
_description_webui_max_login_failures: Number of consecutive failed WebUI login attempts from a single IP before that IP is locked out.
_description_webui_login_lockout_sec: Duration in seconds a client IP remains locked out after exceeding webui_max_login_failures.
_description_webui_auth_session_mode: How the WebUI forces Basic-Auth clients to periodically re-enter credentials: 'legacy' (default) never forces it — the browser keeps sending its cached credential until it exits. 'session_cookie' issues an HMAC-signed, HttpOnly cookie alongside a successful login; once webui_auth_session_timeout_minutes elapses since that cookie was (re)issued, the next request is rejected with 401 (forcing the browser to evict its cached credential and re-prompt) and a fresh cookie is issued so the immediate retry succeeds. 'time_bucket' rotates the WWW-Authenticate realm string every webui_auth_session_timeout_minutes so a browser whose cached credential is keyed to a now-stale realm can no longer auto-supply it and must re-prompt; needs no cookies, but forces every connected client to re-prompt at the same moment.
_description_webui_auth_session_timeout_: Minutes before webui_auth_session_mode ('session_cookie' or 'time_bucket') forces WebUI Basic-Auth clients to re-authenticate. Ignored when webui_auth_session_mode is 'legacy'.
_description_webui_read_header_timeout_s: Seconds the WebUI HTTP server waits for a client to send request headers before closing the connection (Slowloris defence).
_description_webui_read_timeout_sec: Seconds the WebUI HTTP server waits for a complete request body.
_description_webui_write_timeout_sec: Seconds the WebUI HTTP server waits while writing the HTTP response to a client.
_description_webui_idle_timeout_sec: Seconds the WebUI HTTP server keeps an idle keep-alive connection open. Auto-clamped to at least 2x webui_read_timeout_sec.
_description_max_concurrent_dns_tcp_conn: Maximum simultaneous DNS-over-TCP connections. Connections beyond this limit are rejected immediately to bound memory and goroutine count.
_description_max_concurrent_dns_udp_quer: Maximum DNS-over-UDP packets being processed concurrently. Excess packets are dropped rather than queued.
_description_client_tcp_timeout_sec: Per-operation timeout (seconds) for plain DNS TCP connections: reading the 2-byte length header, reading the body, and writing the response each receive this budget independently.
_description_max_recent_blocks: Maximum number of recently blocked domains tracked for the WebUI Blocks page (LRU eviction when full).
_description_local_doh_read_header_timeo: Seconds the local DoH HTTPS listener waits for a client to send HTTP request headers.
_description_local_doh_read_timeout_sec: Seconds the local DoH HTTPS listener waits for a complete HTTP request body.
_description_local_doh_write_timeout_sec: Seconds the local DoH HTTPS listener waits while writing the HTTP response.
_description_local_doh_idle_timeout_sec: Seconds the local DoH HTTPS listener keeps an idle keep-alive connection open. Auto-clamped to at least 2x local_doh_read_timeout_sec.
_description_cert_log_timeout_sec: Timeout (seconds) for the diagnostic TLS probe that logs certificate chain details when an upstream TLS handshake fails.
_description_upstream_dial_timeout_sec: Timeout (seconds) for establishing a new TCP connection to an upstream DoH server.
_description_upstream_client_timeout_sec: Overall timeout (seconds) for a single upstream DoH HTTP request including dial, headers, and body. Must be >= upstream_dial_timeout_sec.
_description_upstream_retry_backoff_ms: Milliseconds to wait between retry attempts to an upstream DoH server after a transient network failure.
_description_upstream_tcp_keepalive_sec: Interval (seconds) for OS-level TCP Keep-Alive probes to detect dead upstream connections.
_description_upstream_h2_read_idle_timeo: Time (seconds) an HTTP/2 connection must be idle before sending a health-check PING. Must be less than upstream_idle_conn_timeout_sec.
_description_upstream_h2_ping_timeout_se: Timeout (seconds) waiting for an HTTP/2 PING response before closing the zombie connection. Must be less than upstream_h2_read_idle_timeout_sec.
_description_server_graceful_shutdown_se: Time (seconds) to wait for active HTTP/DoH connections to finish during a reload or shutdown before forcefully severing them.
_description_upstream_idle_conn_timeout_: Seconds to keep an idle upstream HTTP connection in the pool before closing it.
_description_upstream_max_idle_conns: Global maximum idle upstream HTTP connections kept in the pool across all upstream hosts combined.
_description_upstream_max_idle_conns_per: Maximum idle upstream HTTP connections per upstream host. Auto-clamped to not exceed upstream_max_idle_conns.
_description_doh_max_request_body_bytes: Maximum bytes accepted in an incoming DoH request body, guarding against memory exhaustion from oversized payloads.
_description_dns_udp_buffer_size: Per-packet receive buffer size in bytes for UDP DNS (512–65535). 4096 safely handles modern EDNS0 payloads.
_description_cachejanitor_interval_minut: Interval in minutes at which the DNS cache background janitor sweeps for and removes expired entries.
_description_cache_negative_ttl_sec: Seconds to cache SERVFAIL and other negative upstream responses (respecting RFC 2308 tho), reducing retry storms during upstream outages. 0 means don't cache.
_description_file_writer_max_retries: Maximum number of retries for atomic file writes. (Default: 6)
_description_file_writer_retry_backoff_m: Delay in milliseconds between file write retries. (Default: 100)
_description_blocked_response_ttl_sec: TTL (seconds) embedded in DNS records returned for blocked queries, controlling how long clients cache the block response. 0 means instruct clients not to cache the blocked response at all; blocked responses are also stored in this proxy's own internal cache for this amount for time.
_description_localhosts_override_ttl_sec: TTL (seconds) embedded in DNS records synthesised from the local host-override file (hosts2ip.json), and how long this proxy's own internal cache retains that synthesized response. 0 means don't cache the response internally (every query re-evaluates the override fresh) and instructs clients not to cache it either.
_description_ui_log_max_lines: Maximum log lines shown per page in the WebUI log viewer. Older lines are omitted to prevent excessive RAM usage and browser freezes.
_description_extra_safety: Enable extra defensive checks: duplicate-entry detection in JSON files, power-loss staging files for atomic writes, and strict purging of malformed or duplicate rules on load. Recommended for production.
